root_cause.text: The vulnerability is caused by using non-RCU-safe list deletion (`list_del_init()`) on an RCU-protected list (`rxnet->calls`), allowing a concurrent RCU reader (e.g., `/proc/net/rxrpc/calls`) to encounter corrupted list pointers and enter an infinite loop.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "Fix rxrpc call removal from the rxnet->calls list to use list_del_rcu() rather than list_del_init() to prevent stuffing up reading /proc/net/rxrpc/calls from potentially getting into an infinite loop." The patch changes `list_del_init(&call->link)` to `list_del_rcu(&call->link)` in `rxrpc_put_call()`.

Check for empty list before deletion; part of the operation that leads to the vulnerable deletion, and accesses the RCU-protected list without using RCU-safe primitives.
Initial check of list emptiness; accesses the RCU-protected list head without RCU protection, which after corruption can cause a reader to see stale state.
Loop condition that repeatedly reads the list head; if the list pointers are corrupted by non-RCU-safe deletion, this loop may never terminate.

vuln_statements.explanation: This check precedes the non-RCU-safe deletion and accesses the RCU-protected list without proper synchronization. It is part of the vulnerable path that leads to corruption.
This is the direct cause of the vulnerability. Using list_del_init() on an RCU-protected list corrupts list pointers for concurrent RCU readers, leading to infinite loops in /proc/net/rxrpc/calls.
This initial check of the RCU-protected list head without RCU protection can observe inconsistent state if the list is corrupted by a concurrent non-RCU-safe deletion.
This loop iterates over the RCU-protected list. If list pointers are corrupted by a concurrent list_del_init(), the loop may never terminate, causing an infinite loop for the RCU reader.
